parameters.name: a
parameters.description: Positive inlet mass-flow-to-pressure conversion gain, fitted jointly with the other free parameters by the pressure-rollout least-squares stages described in estimation.

parameters.name: c
parameters.description: Positive outlet pressure-rate scale, fitted jointly by the pressure-rollout criterion. Its units depend on the explicitly normalized outlet law.

parameters.name: m
parameters.description: Curvature exponent of the effective monotone valve conductance, fitted jointly by the pressure-rollout criterion.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Opening scale of the saturating valve characteristic, fitted jointly by the pressure-rollout criterion.

parameters.name: patm
parameters.description: Approximate absolute atmospheric equilibrium from TASK.md; fixed rather than using an empirical intercept so that zero-inlet equilibrium remains exactly atmospheric.

parameters.name: vfull
parameters.description: Full closure is defined by TASK.md as `valve = 100` percent; used to normalize and clip the opening.

parameters.name: pref
parameters.description: Reference pressure unit, one bar, used for dimensional consistency of a continuously fitted pressure exponent.

parameters.name: eps
parameters.description: Positive pressure-drop regularization scale, fitted jointly; gives a finite slope at atmospheric pressure.

parameters.name: nu
parameters.description: Empirical pressure-drop exponent, jointly fitted between the specified sublinear and linear limits; not claimed to uniquely identify a flow regime.

estimation.criterion: Sum of squared free-running pressure errors in bar squared, excluding the initial row of each simulated segment. This matches the scored state and discourages long-horizon drift; the filtered `dp` column is not a final fitting target. A one-sided residual with weight `100` bar*s penalizes a maximum open-valve relaxation slope above `0.5` per second; the final fit is essentially at that boundary.
estimation.data: Final fit: all `1452` rows of `data/train.csv` and all `1454` rows of `data/val.csv`, treated as separate trajectories. Earlier selection fit: first `1000` rows of each file; later rows were excluded at that stage to permit independently initialized contiguous-suffix checks. The validation file was deliberately allowed into final estimation after structure comparison to use both available experiments. For this candidate, final full-trajectory RK4 pressure RMSE was `0.024786824` bar on `data/train.csv` and `0.037505993` bar on `data/val.csv`. Prefix-fitted, independently initialized suffix RMSE was `0.022030271` bar on training-file rows `1000:1452` (zero-based) and `0.061874437` bar on validation-file rows `1000:1454` (zero-based). The maximum full-opening pressure relaxation slope of this fitted law is `0.50001416` per second.
estimation.method: Bound-constrained nonlinear least squares with the trust-region reflective algorithm, `scipy.optimize.least_squares`, using finite-difference Jacobians and `x_scale = "jac"`. This method accommodates nonlinear constitutive parameters and sign constraints; direct ordinary least squares would not minimize pressure-rollout error. Deterministic warm starting used the preceding physically matched fits, with starting values `a = 0.001235139841219475` bar/(s*(l/min)), `c = 0.1987749600201672` 1/s, `m = 1.555570499135385` dimensionless, `k = 0.4245238290090353` dimensionless, `eps = 0.1020821664882549` bar, `nu = 0.5494405095422799` dimensionless. These are numerical starting points taken from `pooled_fits.json` or `stable_fits.json`, not fixed final coefficients. All free parameters of this candidate were fitted together first to both independent trajectory prefixes, then jointly refitted to both full trajectories, starting at that prefix solution. The prefix stage used 45 objective evaluations and the full stage used 18 objective evaluations as reported by SciPy; all stages used at most `240` evaluations, `ftol = 1e-9`, and `xtol = 1e-9`. No random search or stochastic sampling was used, so no seed applies. Bounds and every starting value are recorded in `atmospheric_fits.json` and implemented in the reproduction script. Each simulation uses classical RK4 with a step of `5` s, the current row inputs held constant, and only the segment first pressure as an initial condition; later measured pressures never reset the simulation.

discussion.family: A one-state grey-box isothermal gas mass-balance model: the inlet term increases stored gas mass and the outlet term removes it. Only effective gains, rather than temperature and volume separately, are identifiable. The ideal-gas storage balance is assumed, not inferred from these data. Grey-box identification reference: Ljung, System Identification: Theory for the User, second edition (1999), cited from memory and not source-checked. The outlet is a regularized signed power-law pressure-flow constitutive relation. It is an empirical interpolation between sublinear orifice-like and linear resistance behavior, rather than an exact compressible-flow formula.
discussion.interpretation: `p` is absolute headspace pressure in bar; `valve` is outlet closure in percent; `flow` is the logged inlet flow in l/min; `dp` is the modeled pressure derivative in bar/s. `a` is the fitted positive inlet conversion gain. `a*flow` is inlet pressurization. `patm = 1` bar is the fixed approximate atmospheric pressure, not a measured atmospheric calibration. `vfull = 100` percent is the declared full-closure position. The clipped opening `Max(0, Min(1, 1-valve/vfull))` is dimensionless. `k` is a positive dimensionless opening scale and `m` a positive dimensionless curvature exponent. The monotone saturating characteristic `(Max(0, Min(1, 1-valve/vfull))/(Max(0, Min(1, 1-valve/vfull))+k))**m` represents an effective valve conductance, including the outlet plumbing; it is an empirical calibration law, not a measured geometric area. Clipping prevents unphysical conductance when an input is outside its declared range. `pref = 1` bar is the reference pressure unit. `eps` is the positive regularization pressure and `nu` the dimensionless fitted pressure exponent. The outlet function `(p-patm)*(((p-patm)**2+eps**2)/pref**2)**((nu-1)/2)` has a finite linear slope near atmospheric pressure and a signed power-law dependence at larger departures. `c` has units inverse seconds because this function has units bar. The sublinear exponent describes mathematical curvature; it is not independent evidence of a particular valve-flow regime.
discussion.origin: Physical reasoning supplied the one-state gas inventory balance, a positive term linear in inlet flow, atmospheric pressure as zero outlet driving pressure, and zero outlet conductance at full closure. A deterministic manual structure comparison, not symbolic regression, supplied the saturating opening law. Derivative-target nonlinear least-squares fits initialized the pressure-rollout fits; valve power, exponential, logistic, saturating and series-restriction characteristics were compared. Saturating conductance was retained because it improved pressure prediction without a high-dimensional calibration curve. The regularized square-root and series-resistance fits left pressure- and closure-dependent residuals. A fitted pressure exponent was tried to allow the data to choose curvature instead of fixing it at a square root. This was a manual constitutive extension, not an automated symbolic search. Flow-quadratic extensions collapsed toward zero gain, and a monotone valve calibration curve did not reliably improve held-out suffix predictions, so neither was retained. The equilibrium was fixed at atmospheric pressure and a slope penalty was added for numerical safety.
discussion.limitations: No measured headspace temperature, independently calibrated atmospheric pressure, valve geometry, or standard-flow reference conditions were available. Therefore fitted gains do not separately determine tank volume, temperature, or discharge area. The one-state structure omits bubble residence time, controller lag, valve hysteresis, and sensor dynamics. Both trajectories were used in the final fit, so full-trajectory errors are in-sample diagnostics, not test scores. The suffix checks were not used for parameter estimation at that stage, but were inspected during structure selection, so they are not untouched confirmatory tests. At very large pressure departures, negative absolute pressures, altered water level, or different hardware the model is not established. The data do not cover perfectly sealed operation, exactly zero flow at steady state, or all combinations of pressure and valve opening. The exponent and regularization are phenomenological, and can compensate for unmodeled valve characteristics or filtering. They should not be extrapolated to sonic choking or large changes of pressure or temperature. R1: the flow derivative is `a > 0`, so increasing inlet flow always increases `dp`. R2: on the intended pressurized operating domain `p >= patm`, closing the valve reduces outlet conductance and therefore cannot reduce `dp`. Below atmospheric pressure, ambient backflow restores pressure; closing the valve then reduces that restoration, so R2 cannot hold globally there for this bidirectional-flow model. This is an explicit qualification, not a claimed global monotonicity guarantee. R3: with `flow = 0` and `valve < vfull`, the unique equilibrium is exactly `p = patm = 1` bar. R4: for these same inputs, `dp` has the opposite sign to `p-patm`, giving continuous-time relaxation from either side. R5: at `valve = vfull`, outlet conductance is zero and `dp = a*flow >= 0` for nonnegative supplied flow. No leakage at full closure is assumed; none is identified from the logged range.
